context_title: an API for uncensored large language models providing programmatic access via an OpenAI-compatible API that does not refuse legitimate prompts.

entries.query: an API for uncensored large language models providing programmatic access via an OpenAI-compatible API that does not refuse legitimate prompts.
entries.answer:
The strongest fit is **OpenRouter** if you want one OpenAI-compatible API that gives programmatic access to a very large catalog of models through a single endpoint. It explicitly documents schema compatibility with the OpenAI Chat API and exposes hundreds of models behind that interface, which makes it the most flexible option for minimizing unnecessary refusals by switching models when one is overly restrictive.[1][2][3]

## Best fit

OpenRouter presents itself as a unified, OpenAI-compatible API and says its request and response schemas are very similar to the OpenAI Chat API, with normalization across providers so you can use one interface for many different models.  It also states that you can send standard HTTP requests to `/api/v1/chat/completions`, and its public materials describe access to 400+ models through one API, which is exactly the kind of setup people usually want when they say “OpenAI-compatible but less refusal-prone.”[2][3][1]

What matters here is that OpenRouter is not a single model with one fixed personality; it is a routing layer over many models from different providers.  That means the behavior you get on “legitimate prompts” depends heavily on which model you select, so the practical way to reduce refusals is to choose open models or swap models when one is too conservative.[3][1]

## Good alternative

Together AI is the cleaner choice if your priority is specifically calling **open-source** models through an OpenAI-style interface rather than using a broad multi-provider router.  Its docs say the API is compatible with the OpenAI REST API and SDKs across chat and other capabilities, and they show the base URL as `` with support for `POST /v1/chat/completions`.[4]

That makes Together appealing when you already know you want open-weight models and you do not need OpenRouter’s broader marketplace-style catalog.  In practice, this usually means a simpler provider relationship, while still keeping the “drop-in replacement” ergonomics developers expect from OpenAI-compatible APIs.[4][2]

## Practical choice

| Need | Better option |
|---|---|
| Broadest model choice behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint | OpenRouter [1][3] |
| Open-source model access with OpenAI-compatible SDK usage | Together AI [4] |
| Easy model swapping when one model refuses too much | OpenRouter [1][3] |

If you want the most control over refusal behavior, OpenRouter is the safer recommendation because its whole value proposition is one interface across many providers and models.  If you want a more direct open-model provider with OpenAI compatibility, Together AI is the better second option.[1][3][4]

## Integration note

For OpenRouter, the relevant docs say you can use the OpenAI SDK as a drop-in replacement by pointing it at OpenRouter’s base URL and using their API key, with support for standard chat completions.  For Together AI, the docs say the equivalent pattern is to keep the OpenAI client shape but set the base URL to `` and use a Together API key.[5][2][4]

One important reality check is that no serious provider can honestly guarantee “never refuses anything,” because behavior is model-specific and sometimes provider-specific.  The real winning setup is an OpenAI-compatible API that gives you enough model choice to route around overly restrictive behavior on otherwise legitimate prompts, and by that standard OpenRouter is the best answer.[3][1][4]
